title: Standardized Pre-clinical Surgical Animal Model Protocol for Ischemic Flap Healing
author: Aksamitiene, Heffelfinger, et al.
materials: Personal protective equipment (PPE): surgical gown, ear loop face mask, hair cap, shoe covers, sterile surgical gloves, non-sterile gloves, safety glasses.
Stainless steel instrument tray with flap cover – for autoclaving and storage of surgical instruments
Stainless steel Grafco Flat Type instrument tray – for placing the surgical items during the procedure (Additional File 2, Fig. S1)
Sharps disposal container – for disposal of needles and syringes
Biohazard disposal container and biohazard bags – for safe disposal of biohazardous trash, including pipette tips.
Single or dual-channel anesthesia system with gas vaporizer, inlet flowmeter, charcoal filters, high pressure oxygen hose, oxygen regulator, and low-profile anesthesia masks adapted for rodents.
Handheld hair clipper and/or trimmer (e.g., WAHL for Home Pet).
Isoflurane inhalant anesthetic for veterinary use (USP)

steps.title: Prepare analgesic syringe
steps.instruction: Pre-operative analgesic (opioids such as sustained release buprenorphine hydrochloride are typically obtained from LAS veterinarian staff). Otherwise, take a new sterile 1 ml syringe, slowly draw in analgetic solution into the syringe. Point the syringe upward to bring any air bubbles to the top of the needle. Plunge the syringe slowly to expel any air until only liquid expels from the syringe. Double check volume, place the needle cap and set a syringe aside.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The heating pad is set for 122°F (50 °C) and covered with two surgical underpads.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The anesthesia machines is turned on to prefill the padded rodent sedation chamber with 4–5% induction isoflurane gas.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The animal is placed in the chamber and kept there for up to 4 min.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: 3% isoflurane flow is then redirected into the nose cone attached to the anesthesia machine.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The sedated rat is removed from the chamber and placed onto the heating pad in a prone position.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The lubricate ointment is generously applied onto animal’s eyes.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The rat is placed back into a supine position and its fur is shaved until the nude skin is exposed.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The top surgical pad containing shaved fur is removed.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Shaved skin areas are wiped with betadine solution, which is copiously applied onto a non-woven sponge.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Animal weight is recorded in the post-operative animal monitoring sheet (POAMS) (see Additional File 1).

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The animal is returned to the cage and monitored until awakened.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Appropriate PPE is donned by the surgeon.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The HDPE tubes, 10% formalin-prefilled containers and histology cassettes are labeled for appropriate specimen.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The vascular clamps, that are being stored in enzymatic solution, are removed, washed with distilled water, and then placed in an Eppendorf tube containing 70% alcohol.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The hot glass bead sterilizer is turned on to preheat.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The heating pad is set to reach 122°F (50 °C). It is covered with four surgical underpads: 1 extra-large and 3 medium or small.

steps.title: Place PVA sponge implantation wicks in tissue dish
steps.instruction: If an optional PVA sponge implantation is desired, then two sterile 9 mm × 15 mm ear wicks are placed onto 100 × 20 mm tissue culture dish prefilled with sterile PBS. These wicks are then cut into three pieces per each using a disposable scalpel. The lid of tissue dish is closed to prevent the PVA sponges from drying.

substeps.instruction: Place two sterile 9 mm × 15 mm ear wicks onto 100 × 20 mm tissue culture dish prefilled with sterile PBS
Cut each wick into three pieces using a disposable scalpel
Close the lid of tissue dish to prevent PVA sponges from drying

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The dose of analgesic agent is prepared for each individual animal based on the recorded animal weight (for example, our rats received 1.0–1.2 mg/kg of Buprenorphine-HCl-SR formulation subcutaneously (sc)).

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Dewar flask is prefilled with liquid nitrogen (LN2).

steps.title: Prepare anesthesia gas
steps.instruction: Isoflurane and oxygen tank levels are checked, and the proper amount of isoflurane is added to the gas anesthesia machine chamber before the experiment if needed. The anesthesia machine is turned one to prefill the padded rat sedation chamber with 4–5% isoflurane gas.

substeps.instruction: Check isoflurane tank level
Check oxygen tank level
Add proper amount of isoflurane to the gas anesthesia machine chamber before the experiment if needed
Turn anesthesia machine on to prefill the padded rat sedation chamber with 4–5% isoflurane gas

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The animal is placed into the anesthetic sedation chamber and kept there for up to 4 min.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: 3% isoflurane flow is redirected into the nose cone attached to the anesthesia machine.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The sedated rat is removed from the chamber and placed onto the heating pad in a prone position.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Animal’s eyes are lubricated by applying the ointment, and analgesia is injected sc.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The animal is turned back to the supine position. The use of medical tape for animal stabilization during the flap design procedure is not recommended, as the animal skin should be in the most natural and relaxed condition.

steps.title: Mark flap boundaries
steps.instruction: Flap boundaries are identified by applying a pre-cut cardboard 9.5 × 3 cm flap design template and drawing a single dotted line with a skin marker. After removing the template, a second dotted line is drawn above the first just a few millimeters apart. Finally, a solid line is drawn through the inner dots as shown in Fig. 2A.Fig. 2Design of BEFAF. A Contours for flap elevation and biopsies. B Preparation of flap for baseline biopsy (B0) excision. C Flap pocket after B0 excision is used for blinded dissection and partial separation of fasciocutaneous tissue from the muscle. D Superficial cutting of inner flap sidewalls

substeps.instruction: Place the pre‑cut cardboard template (9.5 × 3 cm) on the flap and draw a single dotted line with a skin marker.
Remove the template.
Draw a second dotted line a few millimeters above the first line.
Draw a solid line through the inner dots (see Fig. 2A).

steps.title: Mark biopsy flap areas
steps.instruction: Flap areas that will be used for the excisional biopsies are then marked. In the example provided herein we defined four 1 × 3 cm biopsy areas:A)B0 – baseline.B)BPI – to be excised after the end of global primary ischemia (PI) and prior to reperfusion.C)BVO – to be excised after the end of secondary venous ischemia.D)BAO – to be excised after the end of secondary arterial ischemia (Fig. 2A).

substeps.instruction: Mark flap areas that will be used for the excisional biopsies
Define four 1 × 3 cm biopsy areas: B0 – baseline
Define BPI – to be excised after the end of global primary ischemia (PI) and prior to reperfusion
Define BVO – to be excised after the end of secondary venous ischemia
Define BAO – to be excised after the end of secondary arterial ischemia

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: An incision on the top of the flap is made using straight Iris Supercut scissors. The cut is deepened. A portion of biopsy area is released from the fascia using Mayo dissecting scissors (Fig. 2B).

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The baseline (B0) biopsy area is lifted using Adson tissue forceps. This portion of skin is then cut out using Metzenbaum-Nelson scissors (Fig. 2C, left panel).

steps.title: Place specimen in histology cassette
steps.instruction: For HIS/IHC, the excised specimen is divided using a straight Iris Supercut scissors. The specimen is placed into a pre-labeled histology cassette, which is submerged in 10% formalin. For long-term tissue storage, the remaining specimen pieces are placed into the pre-labeled HDPE tube, which is sealed and submerged in LN2.

substeps.instruction: Divide excised specimen using straight Iris Supercut scissors
Submerge specimen in 10% formalin
Place remaining specimen pieces in pre-labeled HDPE tube
Seal HDPE tube
Submerge HDPE tube in LN2

steps.title: Dissect tissue under flap
steps.instruction: After a re-entry to the existing pocket, the tissue is dissected underneath the flap by slowly moving Mayo scissors towards the pedicle (Fig. 2C, right panel). It is important not to open the scissors too wide beyond the medial boundaries of the designed flap.

substeps.instruction: After re‑entry to the existing pocket, slowly move Mayo scissors towards the pedicle to dissect tissue underneath the flap.
Do not open the scissors beyond the medial boundaries of the designed flap.

steps.title: Cut flap sidewalls and free fascia
steps.instruction: Straight Iris Supercut or Metzenbaum-Nelson scissors are used to cut through the inner sidewall of the flap up to its end (Fig. 2D, left panel). The same is done for the opposite side (Fig. 2D, right panel). Some portions of the flap may still be attached to the underlying muscle by vascularized fascia (Fig. 3A, left panel). If so, a flap is lifted, and the fascia is cauterized so that the flap can be freed up to its base (Fig. 3A, right panel).

substeps.instruction: Use Straight Iris Supercut or Metzenbaum-Nelson scissors to cut through the inner sidewall of the flap up to its end (Fig. 2D, left panel).
Repeat the cut on the opposite side of the flap (Fig. 2D, right panel).
If any flap portions remain attached by vascularized fascia, lift the flap.
Cauterize the attached fascia to free the flap to its base (Fig. 3A, right panel).

steps.title: Cut through lateral solid line of flap roughly to midline
steps.instruction: Straight Iris Supercut or Metzenbaum-Nelson scissors are used to cut through the lateral solid line of the flap roughly to its midline (Fig. 3C, left panel). From this point forward only the superficial layer of the flap should be cut through to avoid the damage of lateral branch of the SIEA (Fig. 3C, right panel). The same is done for the opposite side.

substeps.instruction: Use Straight Iris Supercut or Metzenbaum-Nelson scissors
Cut through superficial layer of flap to avoid damage of lateral branch of SIEA
Repeat for opposite side

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The cautery device is used to cut through the tissue of the elevated flap until its base (Fig. 3D). The same is done for the opposite side.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Both flaps are returned into their original horizontal position.

steps.title: Wrap flaps in sterile gauze with DPBS
steps.instruction: The pedicle is exposed. Some rats have abundant fatty tissue obscuring a view to the emerging SIEA/SIEV bundle from femoral artery/vein. Such cases require a deeper dissection and removal of more fascia around the thigh and the vessels (Fig. 4A). Once the vessels appear clean, each flap is wrapped in sterile gauze moistened with sterile DPBS to preserve them from drying and return to the original horizontal position (Fig. 4B). NOTE: to minimize variation, the temperature of DPBS should be kept constant unless the objective is to compare the viability of flaps exposed to warm or cold ischemia.

substeps.instruction: Wrap each flap in sterile gauze
Moisten gauze with sterile DPBS
Preserve flaps from drying
Return flaps to original horizontal position

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Isoflurane flow should be decreased to 2%.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Holding the tip and the center portions of the wrapped flap, a flap is positioned over the animal’s thigh so that the pedicle appears in an extended position (Fig. 4C).

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The SIEA and SIEV vessels are irrigated in 1% Lidocaine HCl solution applied dropwise.

steps.title: Examine pedicle vessels closely
steps.instruction: At this point the vessels of the pedicle may be examined more closely. The most suitable site for physical SIEV or SIEA separation is based on vessel anatomy and the surgeon’s left- or right-handedness. Vessel anatomy in male and female rats slightly differs. In contrast to females (Fig. 4D, left panel), male SIEA may be less pronounced and run very close to SIEV without making large loops (Fig. 4D, right panel), which may pose a challenge for their separation without an aid of magnifying spectacles and LED headlight.

steps.title: Isolate SIEV with needle and scissors
steps.instruction: For SIEV isolation the Halsey micro needle holder scissors are used. Once the largest gap between the SIEA and SIEV before the point of SIEV bifurcation is identified (Fig. 5A), a 4–0 size needle with attached silk suture is passed between the SIEA and SIEV in a direction shown in Fig. 5B. When the needle shows on the opposite side of SIEV, the scissors are released. The needle is grabbed close to the tip and slowly pulled upwards until the suture is underneath the SIEV (Fig. 5C). CRITICAL: if one of the vessels gets accidentally punctured, the bleeding can be stopped by clamping, raising both vessels and ligating them with LigaClip tool. When properly ligated and cut in half, vessels should not bleed (see Additional File 2, Fig. S3A and Fig. S3B). A ligated flap may serve as a negative control for BEFAF survival. The flap (right or left) that has been ligated and the time of ligation should be immediately marked in the POAMS “Surgery notes” field (Additional File 1).

substeps.instruction: Use Halsey micro‑needle‑holder scissors.
Identify the largest gap between SIEA and SIEV before the SIEV bifurcation (Fig. 5A).
Pass a 4‑0 needle with attached silk suture between SIEA and SIEV in the direction shown in Fig. 5B.
When the needle tip appears on the opposite side of the SIEV, release the scissors.
Grasp the needle near its tip and slowly pull upward until the suture lies underneath the SIEV (Fig. 5C).
If a vessel is punctured, stop bleeding by clamping, raising both vessels, and ligating with a LigaClip tool.
Verify that ligated and halved vessels do not bleed (see Additional File 2, Fig. S3A/B).
Optionally keep the ligated flap as a negative control for BEFAF survival.
Immediately record the ligated flap side (right or left) and the ligation time in the POAMS “Surgery notes” field (Additional File 1).

steps.title: Tie loose knot around isolated vessel
steps.instruction: The suture is cut, and a loose knot is tied around the isolated vessel (Fig. 5D). NOTE: The 4–0 size needle should make a passage wide enough for a subsequent application of vascular clamp. It is possible to carefully widen this gap by using microscissors and lifting the attached suture loop, but it may increase the risk of vessel damage.

substeps.instruction: Cut suture
Use 4–0 size needle to make passage
Widen gap with microscissors if necessary

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Similarly, the SIEA is separated on the opposite flap (Fig. 5E). If the SIEA forms a significant branch, a suture should pass right before the bifurcation point as shown in Additional File 2, Fig. S3C.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: In the POAMS form (Additional File 1) the “Surgery Notes” field is used to indicate which vessel has been isolated by looping on the left and the right side of the animal.

steps.title: Lift fascia with curved micro forceps
steps.instruction: Slightly or fully curved smooth jaws micro forceps are used to lift fascia. Then Iris microscissors are used to make a small tunnel below the tied loop on the top and bottom of the pedicle (Fig. 6A). This passage is widened by inserting the microscissors underneath the pedicle and slowly opening them to dissect the remaining tissue (Fig. 6B). This step is repeated for the opposite side (Fig. 6C).

substeps.instruction: Use slightly or fully curved smooth jaws micro forceps to lift fascia
Use Iris microscissors to make a small tunnel below the tied loop on the top of the pedicle
Use Iris microscissors to make a small tunnel below the tied loop on the bottom of the pedicle
Insert microscissors underneath the pedicle and slowly open them to dissect the remaining tissue
Repeat for the opposite side

steps.title: Apply vascular clamp and verify occlusion
steps.instruction: Vascular clamp-applying forceps are used to insert one B-2 V vascular clamp onto the pedicle with an already separated SIEV (Fig. 6D). Using slightly curved microforceps, the flow below an applied clamp is gently pushed towards the femoral vein to make sure that the blood outflow from the vein is fully ceased. It is normal to see some backflow from the femoral vein. NOTE: If the venous blood surpasses the clamp, there may be too much fascia left around the vessel. If a problem persists after repositioning of a clamp, a second (smaller) clamp may be applied making sure there is no blood entrapped between the two clamps (see Additional File 2, Fig. S3D).

substeps.instruction: Insert one B-2 V vascular clamp onto the pedicle using clamp‑applying forceps.
With slightly curved microforceps, gently push flow below the clamp toward the femoral vein to stop outflow.
Observe for normal backflow from the femoral vein.
If venous blood passes the clamp, reduce surrounding fascia and reposition the clamp.
If problem persists, apply a second smaller clamp, ensuring no blood is trapped between the two clamps.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Once the clamp is in a proper position, a countdown timer is immediately set and started for the desired duration of the PI (e.g., 4 h).

steps.title: Push blood away from clamp site
steps.instruction: Steps 11 and 12 are repeated for an opposite side. In the case of arterial occlusion, the curved microforceps should be used gently to push blood away from the site of the clamp going distally towards the flap. If the clamp is adequately applied, no influx of blood will be seen in the artery between the clamp and the curved microforceps.

substeps.instruction: Use curved microforceps to push blood distally towards the flap
Apply clamp adequately to prevent blood influx between clamp and microforceps

steps.title: Widen passage with microscissors/cautery
steps.instruction: The flap is held vertically by regular forceps, and the microscissors or fine-tip cautery is used to widen the passage by dissecting tissue along the clamped SIEA/SIEV bundle (Fig. 6E). The angle between the isolated clamped pedicle and the flap should be ~ 45–60°. The same step is repeated for the opposite side.

substeps.instruction: Hold flap vertically by regular forceps
Dissect tissue along clamped SIEA/SIEV bundle
Widen passage to 45–60° angle

steps.title: Return flaps, check gauze moisture, add DPBS if needed
steps.instruction: Both flaps are returned to their original horizontal position. The moisture level of the gauzes that are wrapped around each flap is checked. If needed, an additional amount of sterile DPBS is applied. If the underpad is wet, it should be replaced to avoid hypothermia of the animal.

substeps.instruction: Return both flaps to their original horizontal position
Check the moisture level of the gauzes wrapped around each flap
If needed, apply an additional amount of sterile DPBS
If the underpad is wet, replace it to avoid hypothermia of the animal

steps.title: Cut flap base superficially with Iris Supercut scissors
steps.instruction: At this point the flap is supplied by residual microvascular plexus. To remove this feed the entire base portion of the flap is cut superficially using the Iris Supercut scissors (Fig. 7A). NOTE: this step can be omitted for local/regional pedicled advancement or rotational flaps since these do not simulate a free flap situation.

substeps.instruction: Feed entire base portion of the flap
Use Iris Supercut scissors
Cut superficially

steps.title: Cauterize flap base while holding vertically
steps.instruction: The tissue at the base of the flap is cauterized while holding the flap vertically (Fig. 7B). At this point, the flap becomes connected to the animal only by the clamped pedicle (Fig. 7C). CRITICAL: Without pulling the pedicle (it may cause undue strain on the vessels), the flap is returned into its original horizontal position (Fig. 7D), and this step is repeated for the opposite side.

substeps.instruction: Cauterize tissue at the base of the flap
Hold the flap vertically
Return the flap to its original horizontal position without pulling the pedicle
Repeat for the opposite side

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The 2% isoflurane flow should be decreased to 1%.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The flaps are sutured to the wound boundaries by using buried simple-interrupted suturing technique and non-absorbable silk suture (Additional File 2, Fig. S4) in the order and directions as suggested in Additional File 2, Fig. S5.

steps.title: Suture bottom corners of longer and shorter flaps
steps.instruction: First, the bottom corners of a longer flap (which did not undergo biopsy excision) are sutured, and the same procedure is performed on a shorter flap (Additional File 2, Fig. S6). It is important to begin by suturing the base of the flap in order to minimize strain on the vascular pedicle.

substeps.instruction: Suture the bottom corners of a longer flap
Suture the bottom corners of a shorter flap (Additional File 2, Fig. S6)
Begin by suturing the base of the flap to minimize strain on the vascular pedicle

steps.title: Suture flap corners and center
steps.instruction: Second, the upper corners of a longer flap are sutured followed by the center (Fig. 7E, left panel) and the remaining suturing points at the gaps (Fig. 7E, middle panel). A water-tight closure of the top and bottom parts of the flap is not necessary, but enough to prevent exposure of the clamp or vessel isolation loop and excessive accumulation of blood onto the future biopsies (Fig. 7E, right panel).

substeps.instruction: Suture the upper corners of the longer flap
Suture the center of the flap
Suture the remaining points at the gaps

steps.title: Suture flap with non-absorbable silk suture
steps.instruction: On the opposite side, the upper corners of a shorter flap are sutured using a non-absorbable silk suture. Finally, the center and the remaining points are sutured using an absorbable suture. NOTE: the guiding dots for suturing of this flap will not exactly match since the flap will be slightly advanced (Fig. 7F).

substeps.instruction: Suture upper corners of shorter flap using non-absorbable silk suture
Suture center and remaining points using absorbable suture

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Isoflurane flow is decreased to 0% so that the animal would receive 100% oxygen. When it starts showing the signs of awakening on the operating table, it is returned to a cage to recover.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The instruments are cleaned from blood and dry-sterilized using the hot bead Germinator.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: All waste is removed, and sharps are disposed in specified containers.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The cage is kept in the vicinity to monitor the animal’s well-being and activities more closely. If it starts extensively picking on the sutures, the Elizabethan collar should be applied.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Fifteen minutes prior to the planned end of PI, the animal is placed into the anesthetic chamber for up to 4 min.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Meanwhile, two new underpads are placed onto a heating pad.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: 3% isoflurane flow is redirected into the nose cone.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The sedated animal is removed from the chamber and placed onto the heating pad in a prone position. The lubricate ointment is applied onto both eyes prior to turning the animal over in a supine position.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Isoflurane flow is adjusted to the maintaining 2% (for larger animal) or 1% (for smaller animal).

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The flaps are gently wiped with DPBS-moistened gauze pad to remove any aggregated blood. Then the top underpad can be removed.

steps.title: Inspect ischemia visually
steps.instruction: The degree of ischemia is inspected visually in both flaps. After 2 h of PI, flap color should be significantly darker than the surrounding skin, and even more so after 4 h of PI (Fig. 8A). NOTE: if the color does not significantly differ, it may indicate that the vascular clamping was insufficient or ineffective. With the extent of usage, the gripping power of reusable clamps gets weaker, and caution must be taken to prevent the clamp from falling off the pedicle in an active animal.

substeps.instruction: Observe flap color at 2 h post‑ischemia (PI); it should be significantly darker than surrounding skin
Observe flap color at 4 h post‑ischemia (PI); it should be even darker than at 2 h
If color does not differ, note possible insufficient or ineffective vascular clamping
Check that reusable clamp grip remains secure; prevent clamp from falling off pedicle in the active animal

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The suture is disrupted at points #4, #5, #6, #17 and #18 from the top portion of the longer (in this example, left) flap, followed by excision of the BPI biopsy (Fig. 8B).

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The sutures are removed from points #1 and # 9 (also #3 if needed more space) at the lower midline and an inner corner of the flap base on both sides (Fig. 8C, left panel).

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Left flap is gently lifted (Fig. 8C, right panel) to remove the clamp by gripping it with the vascular clamp-applying forceps.

steps.title: Observe pedicle for blood flow
steps.instruction: The pedicle is observed for restored blood flow (Fig. 8D). NOTE: we take note whether, upon clamp removal, there is some movement of venous blood. Small thrombi, if any, can be removed by applying a gentle sliding force with non-serrated microforceps. The vessels can be irrigated with 1% Lidocaine HCl solution applied dropwise after touching the pedicle.

substeps.instruction: Note movement of venous blood upon clamp removal
Remove small thrombi with gentle sliding force using non-serrated microforceps
Irrigate vessels with 1% Lidocaine HCl solution applied dropwise after touching the pedicle

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Once the blood shows a sign of flow within the pedicle, the countdown timer is set and started for the desired primary reperfusion (REP1) interval (e. g. 2 h).

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Steps 9 to 13 are repeated for the right flap. Then, flap corners are sutured back to their original position using silk suture.

steps.title: Repair left flap sutures
steps.instruction: The remaining sutures on the left flap are disrupted. The top portion is reconnected to the tissue using silk suture. IMPORTANT: Then, an absorbable suture is used to connect the center and remaining parts so that both flaps are advanced equally.

substeps.instruction: Disrupt remaining sutures on left flap
Reconnect top portion to tissue with silk suture
Connect center and remaining parts with absorbable suture to advance both flaps equally

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Steps 6 to 9 from “Partial flap closure” section are repeated.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Fifteen minutes prior to the planned end of REP1, the animal is anesthetized and prepared for the procedure as described previously.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: 3% (for larger animal) or 2% (for smaller animal) isoflurane flow is redirected to the nose cone.

steps.title: Visually inspect flaps
steps.instruction: The appearance of both flaps is visually inspected to assess the approximate percent of restored blood flow. Figure 9A shows a case of efficient (~ 73%) reperfusion of a flap only 2 h after a designated 4 h PI time, which is well above the expected average [78].

substeps.instruction: Inspect the appearance of both flaps
Estimate the approximate percent of restored blood flow

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The suturing points #2, #3 and #10 are disrupted at the lower sidewall and outer corners of flap base on both sides (Fig. 9B).

steps.title: Inspect flap blood flow
steps.instruction: Left flap is gently lifted to inspect whether the blood flow is fully restored in the pedicle (Fig. 9C). Caution: some animals may develop spontaneous arterial or venous or mixed thrombosis after the PI (Additional File 2, Fig. S7). If a drop of heparin and 1% lidocaine does not resolve the thrombus and if the flow is not restored after a gentle push toward the groin area, the flap will be lost and should be excluded from the study. In such case, an opposite flap may be used as 4 h PI data point or any selected SI data point without a matching pair.

substeps.instruction: Gently lift left flap and inspect pedicle for restored blood flow
Apply one drop of heparin and 1% lidocaine to the flap
Gently push the flap toward the groin area
If flow is not restored, exclude the flap from the study
Use the opposite flap as a 4 h post‑injury (PI) data point or any selected SI data point

steps.title: Apply vascular clamp and start timer
steps.instruction: B-1 V vascular clamp is applied onto an isolated SIEV (Fig. 9D). While applying the clamp, the suture that separates both vessels is removed. The timer is set and started for desired venous occlusion (VO) period (e. g. 4 h).

substeps.instruction: Apply B-1 V vascular clamp to isolated SIEV (Fig 9D).
While clamping, remove the suture separating the vessels.
Set timer and start for the desired venous occlusion period (e.g., 4 h).

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: B-2 V vascular clamp is immediately applied onto an isolated SIEA on the opposite side. The timer is set and started for desired arterial occlusion (AO) period (e. g. 4 h).

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The bottom of both flaps is then closed using silk sutures.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Steps 6 to 9 from “Partial flap closure” section are repeated.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Fifteen minutes prior to the planned end of AO/VO, the animal is anesthetized and prepared for the procedure as described previously.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: 2% (for larger animal) or 1% (for smaller animal) isoflurane flow is redirected to the nose cone.

steps.title: Examine flap appearance for SI efficacy
steps.instruction: The appearance of the flaps is examined to evaluate the efficacy of SI. VO flap should look significantly darker than AO flap (Fig. 9E). VO flap may be thickened by accumulated blood, which may form dark aggregates around the edges of the flap. These aggregates can be removed by flap irrigation with DPBS.

substeps.instruction: Evaluate the appearance of the VO flap
Ensure VO flap looks significantly darker than AO flap
Check for thickened areas due to accumulated blood
Remove dark aggregates by irrigating flap with DPBS

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The sutures from the top portions of both left and right flaps are disrupted to excise the BVO and BAO biopsies, respectively (Fig. 9F).

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The entire bottom of both flaps is opened widely to remove the clamps. The time of clamp removal is immediately indicated in the POAMS form to track the timing of secondary reperfusion (REP2).

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The pedicles are observed for the restored flow. The thrombi are removed if needed, and both vessels are irrigated in 1% Lidocaine HCl applied dropwise.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The bottom of both flaps is sutured using an absorbable suture.

steps.title: Suture wound bed tissue
steps.instruction: The top of naïve wound bed tissue is narrowed by suturing the upper corners together (Fig. 9G, left panel). The top corners and top middle of each flap are connected to a narrowed tissue using an absorbable suture. Here one may use the corner stitch mattress suturing technique [79]. Next, the center and remaining intermediate points (Fig. 9G, middle panel) are connected together. The same is done for the opposite side.

substeps.instruction: Suture the upper corners of the wound bed together to narrow the top.
Using an absorbable suture, connect each flap’s top corners and top middle to the narrowed tissue (corner‑stitch mattress technique).
Suture the center and remaining intermediate points together.
Repeat the previous suturing on the opposite side.

steps.title: Implant PVA sponge using Adson forceps
steps.instruction: At this point, PVA sponge implantation may take place. One PVA piece is inserted using Adson forceps underneath the P, M and D portions of each flap. Control sponges may be inserted in the outer area of a flap. Alternatively, a small pocket may be opened on the animal’s back.

substeps.instruction: Insert one PVA piece underneath the P, M, and D portions of each flap using Adson forceps.
Insert control sponges in the outer area of a flap.
Alternatively, open a small pocket on the animal’s back.

steps.title: Suture left flap and cover
steps.instruction: A DPBS-moistened gauze is placed over the right flap. The left flap is positioned into place using a running suture technique with non-absorbable permanent suture (suggested directions of suturing are presented in Additional File 2, Fig. S8). The left flap is kept moistened and covered while the opposite side is sutured. NOTE: we do not recommend using proximate skin staplers with rotating head (e.g., Ethicon, #PRR35) to close the wound, especially in female rats that have thin and delicate skin.

substeps.instruction: Place DPBS‑moistened gauze over right flap.
Position left flap and suture using a running non‑absorbable permanent suture (see Additional File 2, Fig. S8).
Keep left flap moistened and covered while suturing the opposite side.
Do not use proximate skin staplers with rotating head (e.g., Ethicon #PRR35), especially for female rats with thin, delicate skin.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The flaps and surrounding areas are wiped with moistened gauze to remove the traces of blood and betadine solution.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The animal is flipped into a prone position. 10 mL of saline is injected sc to supplement bodily fluids lost in the animal during this extensive surgical procedure.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Isoflurane flow is decreased to 0% so that the animal receives only 100% Oxygen.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The gross appearance of the flaps is recorded by digital photography (Fig. 9G, right panel).

steps.title: Apply Elizabethan collar
steps.instruction: Once the animal begins to awaken, we typically put a protective Elizabethan collar prior to returning the animal to a new padded cage with fresh food and water (Additional File 2, Fig. S9). The collar should be applied loosely so that it rotates around the neck.

substeps.instruction: When the animal awakens, loosely place a protective Elizabethan collar so it can rotate around the neck
Return the animal to a fresh padded cage with new food and water

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The HDPE tubes with collected tissue specimen are placed in -80°C freezer for storage.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: All waste is removed, sharps disposed in specified containers, and all surgical instruments are washed, cleaned, and autoclaved at this point.

steps.title: Label HDPE tubes
steps.instruction: The HDPE tubes are labeled for appropriate specimen. A suggested label may contain a unique animal number, code for treatment, indication of left or right flap side (R/L), day of harvest and an abbreviated name of a harvested segment, e.g., “174,871, A, L7D”).

substeps.instruction: Label HDPE tubes for appropriate specimen
Include unique animal number, treatment code, R/L side, day of harvest, and abbreviated segment name (e.g., “174,871, A, L7D”) on each label

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: 10% buffered formalin container and histology cassettes are labeled for appropriate specimen.

steps.title: Prepare ice bucket and tubes
steps.instruction: A rubber bucket is filled with ice pellets. If PVA sponges were implanted, then 2.0 mL Eppendorf tubes are filled with PVA sponge lysis or other buffer, depending on the type of subsequent wound exudate (WE) analysis, and placed on ice. Flat-tip tweezers are prepared to handle the sponges.

substeps.instruction: Fill rubber bucket with ice pellets.
If PVA sponges were implanted, fill 2.0 mL Eppendorf tubes with PVA sponge lysis buffer or other buffer as required for the planned wound exudate analysis, and place the tubes on ice.
Prepare flat‑tip tweezers for handling the sponges.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Dewar flask is prefilled with LN2 for immediate tissue freezing. We suggest using curved HDPE tube grabbing scissors.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: CO2 levels are checked in the euthanasia cart. Isoflurane and oxygen tank levels are checked in the anesthesia cart.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: The animal is placed in the anesthetic sedation chamber prefilled with 4–5% isoflurane gas and kept there for up to 4 min.

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: 4% (larger rats) or 3% (smaller rats) isoflurane flow is redirected into the nose cone.

steps.title: Capture flap images and assess outcome
steps.instruction: Once the animal is placed onto an underpad, which covers a heating pad, the digital photos of the flap appearance are taken. The functional outcome (full survival, partial failure, or total loss) of flaps exposed to SI should be evident by day 5, whereas flap fate following other treatments may be evaluated at later end-points. Figure 10A illustrates experimental situations, when the evaluation of flap survival percentage (FS%) by digital planimetry is not necessary (Fig. 10A, left panel – left flap, middle panel – both flaps) and when it is required (Fig. 10A, right panel – both flaps).

substeps.instruction: Place the animal onto an underpad that covers a heating pad
Take digital photos of the flap appearance
For flaps exposed to SI, evaluate functional outcome (full survival, partial failure, or total loss) by day 5
For flaps with other treatments, evaluate functional outcome at later end‑points

steps.title: Mark flaps for segmentation
steps.instruction: If the flaps are going to be divided into the proximal (P), medial (M) and distal (D) segments, a measuring ruler is placed on the top of a flap. Each flap is marked with either one dot, dotted or a solid line that would separate it into three equal portions. NOTE: this step should be performed on a living animal when the flaps are in fully extended position. If needed, the animal paws may be taped. If the IHC specimen is to be taken out of each portion, then two horizontal lines are drawn along the entire flap as shown in Fig. 10B.

substeps.instruction: Place a measuring ruler on the top of a flap.
Mark each flap with one dot, dotted, or a solid line to separate it into three equal portions.
Ensure this step is performed on a living animal with flaps in fully extended position.
Tape the animal paws if needed.
Draw two horizontal lines along the entire flap if IHC specimen is to be taken out of each portion.

steps.title: Disrupt sutures, dissect flaps, inspect pedicle
steps.instruction: All running sutures are disrupted and removed. One-by-one, the flaps are dissected along the wound margins and Mayo scissors are used to lift one flap after another from the wound bed. The status of the pedicle is inspected and POAMS form (Additional File 1) is used to indicate if it is functional or compromised. A fully functional vessel will be visibly dilated and pumping the blood (Fig. 10C). Obstructed vessel will have a dark blood clot or will be clear of the blood.

substeps.instruction: Disrupt all running sutures
Remove disrupted sutures
Dissect flaps one-by-one along wound margins
Use Mayo scissors to lift each flap from wound bed
Inspect status of pedicle
Use POAMS form to indicate pedicle status (functional or compromised)
Identify a fully functional vessel by visible dilation and blood pumping
Identify an obstructed vessel by dark blood clot or absence of blood

steps.title: Retrieve and clean PVA sponges
steps.instruction: At this point, all PVA sponges may be retrieved if any were implanted previously. These sponges should be cleaned from the tissue prior to placing them into the pre-labeled Eppendorf tubes stored on ice. WE is collected though repeated compression of each sponge with flap-tip tweezers, and the samples are diluted if necessary.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve all PVA sponges if implanted previously
Clean sponges from the tissue
Place cleaned sponges into pre-labeled Eppendorf tubes stored on ice
Collect WE by repeated compression of each sponge with flap-tip tweezers
Dilute samples if necessary

steps.title: Divide flap into P, M, D regions
steps.instruction: If the flap is going to be divided into the P, M and D regions as shown in Fig. 10D, it should preferably be cut into the thirds while it is still attached to the pedicle. Alternatively, the entire flap may be cut at the base, transferred onto a sterile Petri dish kept on ice and divided over there. Optionally, the pedicle can be excised out of the P region for a separate histological evaluation of other types of analysis. Whichever technique the surgeon chooses, he/she should stay consistent and adhere to the chosen sequence of flap harvest procedure throughout the entire course of experiment.

substeps.instruction: Cut flap into thirds while attached to pedicle
Alternatively, cut entire flap at base
Transfer flap onto a sterile Petri dish kept on ice
Divide flap into P, M, D regions on Petri dish
Optionally, excise pedicle out of P region for histological evaluation

steps.title: Prepare IHC tissue cassette
steps.instruction: For IHC, the middle longitudinal strip is cut out of each flap’s segment (Fig. 10E). A specimen is placed into a dedicated IHC casette skin facing up. Edema will be the most prominent in the P segment of the flap, making it the thickest segment out of three. CRITICAL: the tissue strip should be laid straight and should not be twisted. The cassette is submerged in 10% formalin and incubated at RT for at least 48 h.

substeps.instruction: Cut the middle longitudinal strip from each flap segment.
Place the strip into a dedicated IHC cassette, skin side up.
Lay the tissue strip straight, ensuring it is not twisted.
Submerge the cassette in 10% formalin and incubate at RT for ≥48 h.

steps.title: Place flap segment in tube
steps.instruction: The remaining flap segment is placed in a pre-labeled HDPE tube, which is then submerged in LN2. Even though the tissue may be small compared to the volume of the tube, it will less likely stick to the walls of the tube and will be easier to retrieve after freezing.

substeps.instruction: Place the remaining flap segment in the pre‑labeled HDPE tube.
Submerge the tube in liquid nitrogen (LN2).

steps.title: Materials and Methods
steps.instruction: Other flap segments are processed in the same manner as described above.

steps.title: Perform organ harvest and euthanasia
steps.instruction: For major vital organ harvest 5% (or greater) isoflurane flow is used to overdose the animal and then excise all organs of interest after its exsanguination. If organ harvesting is not required, then the gauze is placed over both excisional wounds and the animal is moved into the clean cage for euthanasia. The CO2 flow rate is adjusted at 5 L/min and exposure to CO2 is continued for at least five minutes after respiratory arrest. Euthanasia may be confirmed by cervical dislocation (for rats < 200 g in weight) or bilateral thoracotomy. NOTE: other methods of euthanasia may be used as per approved IACUC study protocol.

substeps.instruction: Overdose animal with ≥5% isoflurane flow
Excise all organs of interest after exsanguination
If no organ harvest, place gauze over excisional wounds and move animal to clean cage
Adjust CO2 flow to 5 L/min
Continue CO2 exposure for ≥5 min after respiratory arrest
Confirm euthanasia by cervical dislocation (rats <200 g) or bilateral thoracotomy
Use alternative approved euthanasia method per IACUC protocol if desired

steps.title: Dispose of animal carcass in biohazardous waste bag
steps.instruction: Animal carcass is placed in a biohazardous waste bag, which is disposed of according to Institutional LAS rules. Typically, this entails attaching a label with a specific information, logging animal death, leaving a carcass in a dedicated freezer or cold room, and concluding a unique animal cage tag.

substeps.instruction: Attach label with specific information
Log animal death
Leave carcass in dedicated freezer or cold room
Conclude unique animal cage tag

steps.title: Prepare animal for flap surgery
steps.instruction: To reduce the time of animal exposure to anesthesia during the major survival surgery, and to minimize the risk of overlapping PI or SI time between the sequentially operated animals, the animals are shaved 16—24 h prior to flap raising procedure:The heating pad is set for 122°F (50 °C) and covered with two surgical underpads.The anesthesia machines is turned on to prefill the padded rodent sedation chamber with 4–5% induction isoflurane gas.The animal is placed in the chamber and kept there for up to 4 min.3% isoflurane flow is then redirected into the nose cone attached to the anesthesia machine.The sedated rat is removed from the chamber and placed onto the heating pad in a prone position.The lubricate ointment is generously applied onto animal’s eyes.The rat is placed back into a supine position and its fur is shaved until the nude skin is exposed.The top surgical pad containing shaved fur is removed.Shaved skin areas are wiped with betadine solution, which is copiously applied onto a non-woven sponge.Animal weight is recorded in the post-operative animal monitoring sheet (POAMS) (see Additional File 1).The animal is returned to the cage and monitored until awakened.

substeps.instruction: Shave animal 16–24 h before flap‑raising procedure.
Set heating pad to 122 °F (50 °C) and cover with two surgical underpads.
Turn on anesthesia machine and prefill padded rodent sedation chamber with 4–5 % induction isoflurane.
Place animal in chamber for up to 4 min.
Redirect 3 % isoflurane flow to nose cone attached to anesthesia machine.
Remove sedated rat and place prone on heating pad.
Apply generous lubricating ointment to the animal’s eyes.
Re‑position rat supine and shave fur until nude skin is exposed.
Remove top surgical pad containing shaved fur.
Wipe shaved skin with betadine‑soaked non‑woven sponge, applying copiously.
Record animal weight in the post‑operative animal monitoring sheet (POAMS).
Return animal to cage and monitor until awakened.

steps.title: Shave animal on surgery day
steps.instruction: NOTE: If less than three consecutive animal surgeries are anticipated one after the other within the same day, animal shaving should be performed on the same day as major survival surgery without an animal being awakened. With experience and proper equipment, animal fur clipping takes less than 12 min. Chemical hair removal creams such as “Nair” are not recommended as they may affect both baseline and injury-inducible biological molecule distribution and/or expression patterns, cause skin irritation or allergic reaction.

substeps.instruction: If less than three consecutive surgeries are anticipated, shave the animal on the same day as the major survival surgery without awakening the animal
Clip fur (takes less than 12 min) using proper equipment
Do not use chemical hair removal creams such as “Nair”

steps.title: Experimental Animal Preparation for Survival Surgery
steps.instruction: The heating pad is set for 122°F (50 °C) and covered with two surgical underpads.

steps.title: Experimental Animal Preparation for Survival Surgery
steps.instruction: The anesthesia machines is turned on to prefill the padded rodent sedation chamber with 4–5% induction isoflurane gas.

steps.title: Experimental Animal Preparation for Survival Surgery
steps.instruction: The animal is placed in the chamber and kept there for up to 4 min.

steps.title: Experimental Animal Preparation for Survival Surgery
steps.instruction: 3% isoflurane flow is then redirected into the nose cone attached to the anesthesia machine.

steps.title: Experimental Animal Preparation for Survival Surgery
steps.instruction: The sedated rat is removed from the chamber and placed onto the heating pad in a prone position.

steps.title: Experimental Animal Preparation for Survival Surgery
steps.instruction: The lubricate ointment is generously applied onto animal’s eyes.

steps.title: Experimental Animal Preparation for Survival Surgery
steps.instruction: The rat is placed back into a supine position and its fur is shaved until the nude skin is exposed.

steps.title: Experimental Animal Preparation for Survival Surgery
steps.instruction: The top surgical pad containing shaved fur is removed.

steps.title: Experimental Animal Preparation for Survival Surgery
steps.instruction: Shaved skin areas are wiped with betadine solution, which is copiously applied onto a non-woven sponge.

steps.title: Experimental Animal Preparation for Survival Surgery
steps.instruction: Animal weight is recorded in the post-operative animal monitoring sheet (POAMS) (see Additional File 1).

steps.title: Experimental Animal Preparation for Survival Surgery
steps.instruction: The animal is returned to the cage and monitored until awakened.

steps.title: Prepare surgical setup and anesthesia
steps.instruction: Appropriate PPE is donned by the surgeon.The HDPE tubes, 10% formalin-prefilled containers and histology cassettes are labeled for appropriate specimen.The vascular clamps, that are being stored in enzymatic solution, are removed, washed with distilled water, and then placed in an Eppendorf tube containing 70% alcohol.The hot glass bead sterilizer is turned on to preheat.The heating pad is set to reach 122°F (50 °C). It is covered with four surgical underpads: 1 extra-large and 3 medium or small.If an optional PVA sponge implantation is desired, then two sterile 9 mm × 15 mm ear wicks are placed onto 100 × 20 mm tissue culture dish prefilled with sterile PBS. These wicks are then cut into three pieces per each using a disposable scalpel. The lid of tissue dish is closed to prevent the PVA sponges from drying.The dose of analgesic agent is prepared for each individual animal based on the recorded animal weight (for example, our rats received 1.0–1.2 mg/kg of Buprenorphine-HCl-SR formulation subcutaneously (sc)).Dewar flask is prefilled with liquid nitrogen (LN2).Isoflurane and oxygen tank levels are checked, and the proper amount of isoflurane is added to the gas anesthesia machine chamber before the experiment if needed. The anesthesia machine is turned one to prefill the padded rat sedation chamber with 4–5% isoflurane gas.

substeps.instruction: Don appropriate PPE.
Label HDPE tubes, 10% formalin containers, and histology cassettes for each specimen.
Remove vascular clamps from enzymatic solution, wash with distilled water, and place in an Eppendorf tube containing 70% alcohol.
Turn on hot glass bead sterilizer to preheat.
Set heating pad to 122 °F (50 °C) and cover with four surgical underpads (1 extra‑large and 3 medium/small).
(Optional) Place two sterile 9 mm × 15 mm ear wicks onto a 100 mm × 20 mm tissue‑culture dish prefilled with sterile PBS.
Cut each wick into three pieces using a disposable scalpel.
Close the dish lid to prevent PVA sponges from drying.
Prepare analgesic dose of Buprenorphine‑HCl‑SR at 1.0–1.2 mg/kg subcutaneously based on each animal’s weight.
Prefill Dewar flask with liquid nitrogen (LN₂).
Check isoflurane and oxygen tank levels; add required isoflurane to the anesthesia machine chamber if needed.
Turn on anesthesia machine to prefill the padded rat sedation chamber with 4–5 % isoflurane gas.

steps.title: Prepare PVA sponge implantation
steps.instruction: If an optional PVA sponge implantation is desired, then two sterile 9 mm × 15 mm ear wicks are placed onto 100 × 20 mm tissue culture dish prefilled with sterile PBS. These wicks are then cut into three pieces per each using a disposable scalpel. The lid of tissue dish is closed to prevent the PVA sponges from drying.

Cut each wick into three pieces using a disposable scalpel
Close the lid of the tissue dish to prevent the PVA sponges from drying

steps.title: Preparation
steps.instruction: The dose of analgesic agent is prepared for each individual animal based on the recorded animal weight (for example, our rats received 1.0–1.2 mg/kg of Buprenorphine-HCl-SR formulation subcutaneously (sc)).

steps.title: Preparation
steps.instruction: Dewar flask is prefilled with liquid nitrogen (LN2).

steps.title: Check isoflurane and oxygen tank levels
steps.instruction: Isoflurane and oxygen tank levels are checked, and the proper amount of isoflurane is added to the gas anesthesia machine chamber before the experiment if needed. The anesthesia machine is turned one to prefill the padded rat sedation chamber with 4–5% isoflurane gas.

substeps.instruction: Check isoflurane tank levels
Check oxygen tank levels
Add proper amount of isoflurane to gas anesthesia machine chamber if needed
Turn on anesthesia machine to prefill padded rat sedation chamber
Set isoflurane gas to 4–5%

steps.title: Prepare labeling and cooling materials
steps.instruction: The HDPE tubes are labeled for appropriate specimen. A suggested label may contain a unique animal number, code for treatment, indication of left or right flap side (R/L), day of harvest and an abbreviated name of a harvested segment, e.g., “174,871, A, L7D”).10% buffered formalin container and histology cassettes are labeled for appropriate specimen.A rubber bucket is filled with ice pellets. If PVA sponges were implanted, then 2.0 mL Eppendorf tubes are filled with PVA sponge lysis or other buffer, depending on the type of subsequent wound exudate (WE) analysis, and placed on ice. Flat-tip tweezers are prepared to handle the sponges.Dewar flask is prefilled with LN2 for immediate tissue freezing. We suggest using curved HDPE tube grabbing scissors.CO2 levels are checked in the euthanasia cart. Isoflurane and oxygen tank levels are checked in the anesthesia cart.

substeps.instruction: Label each HDPE tube for the specimen (e.g., animal number, treatment code, side R/L, day of harvest, segment abbreviation such as “174,871, A, L7D”).
Label the 10% buffered formalin container and histology cassettes for the appropriate specimen.
Fill a rubber bucket with ice pellets.
If PVA sponges were implanted, fill 2.0 mL Eppendorf tubes with PVA sponge lysis buffer (or other appropriate buffer) and place the tubes on ice.
Prepare flat‑tip tweezers for handling the sponges.
Prefill a Dewar flask with liquid nitrogen (LN₂) for immediate tissue freezing; have curved HDPE‑tube‑grabbing scissors ready.
Check CO₂ levels in the euthanasia cart.
Check isoflurane and oxygen tank levels in the anesthesia cart.

steps.title: Label HDPE tubes for specimens
steps.instruction: The HDPE tubes are labeled for appropriate specimen. A suggested label may contain a unique animal number, code for treatment, indication of left or right flap side (R/L), day of harvest and an abbreviated name of a harvested segment, e.g., “174,871, A, L7D”).

substeps.instruction: Label each HDPE tube with a unique animal number
Include a code for treatment on the label
Indicate left or right flap side (R/L)
Add day of harvest to the label
Include an abbreviated name of a harvested segment, e.g., '174,871, A, L7D'

steps.title: Preparation for Procedure
steps.instruction: 10% buffered formalin container and histology cassettes are labeled for appropriate specimen.

steps.title: Prepare ice and lysis tubes
steps.instruction: A rubber bucket is filled with ice pellets. If PVA sponges were implanted, then 2.0 mL Eppendorf tubes are filled with PVA sponge lysis or other buffer, depending on the type of subsequent wound exudate (WE) analysis, and placed on ice. Flat-tip tweezers are prepared to handle the sponges.

substeps.instruction: Fill a rubber bucket with ice pellets.
If PVA sponges were implanted, fill 2.0 mL Eppendorf tubes with PVA sponge lysis or other buffer appropriate for the planned wound exudate (WE) analysis, then place the tubes on ice.
Prepare flat‑tip tweezers for handling the sponges.

steps.title: Preparation for Procedure
steps.instruction: Dewar flask is prefilled with LN2 for immediate tissue freezing. We suggest using curved HDPE tube grabbing scissors.

steps.title: Preparation for Procedure
steps.instruction: CO2 levels are checked in the euthanasia cart. Isoflurane and oxygen tank levels are checked in the anesthesia cart.
